description: Loops, loop control statements and nested loops in C

questions.questionText: Which loop is generally preferred when the number of iterations is known in advance?
questions.explanation: A for loop is commonly used when the initialization, condition and update of a loop can be specified together.

questions.questionText: Which loop is guaranteed to execute its body at least once?
questions.explanation: The condition of a do-while loop is checked after executing the loop body, so it executes at least once.

questions.questionText: Which part of a for loop is executed only once at the beginning?
questions.explanation: The initialization expression of a for loop is executed once before the first iteration.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) printf("%d ", i);
questions.explanation: The loop starts from 1 and continues while i is less than or equal to 5, so it prints 1 through 5.

questions.questionText: How many times will this loop execute? for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++)
questions.explanation: The values of i are 0 through 9, giving a total of 10 iterations.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int i = 1; while (i <= 3) { printf("%d ", i); i++; }
questions.explanation: The loop prints 1, 2 and 3. After i becomes 4, the condition becomes false.

questions.questionText: What happens if the condition of a while loop is initially false?
questions.optionC: The loop body does not execute
questions.explanation: A while loop checks its condition before executing its body, so a false initial condition means zero iterations.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int i = 5; do { printf("%d", i); i++; } while (i < 5);
questions.explanation: A do-while loop executes its body once before checking the condition. After printing 5, i becomes 6 and the condition 6 < 5 is false.

questions.questionText: Which keyword is used to terminate a loop immediately?
questions.explanation: The break statement immediately terminates the nearest enclosing loop.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if (i == 3) break; printf("%d ", i); }
questions.explanation: When i becomes 3, break terminates the loop before printf executes for that iteration.

questions.questionText: Which keyword skips the remaining statements of the current iteration and moves to the next iteration?
questions.explanation: The continue statement skips the remaining part of the current iteration and proceeds to the next iteration.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if (i == 3) continue; printf("%d ", i); }
questions.explanation: When i is 3, continue skips printf for that iteration. Therefore 3 is not printed.

questions.questionText: Which loop is commonly used when the number of iterations depends on a condition evaluated before each iteration?
questions.explanation: A while loop is suitable when the loop continues based on a condition checked before each iteration.

questions.questionText: What is a nested loop?
questions.optionD: A loop containing only if statements
questions.explanation: A nested loop is a loop placed inside the body of another loop.

questions.questionText: How many times does the inner loop execute in total? for (int i = 1; i <= 2; i++) { for (int j = 1; j <= 3; j++) { } }
questions.explanation: The outer loop runs 2 times and the inner loop runs 3 times for each outer iteration, giving 2 × 3 = 6 executions.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 3; i++) printf("*");
questions.explanation: The loop executes three times, and each iteration prints one asterisk.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? for (int i = 5; i >= 1; i--) printf("%d ", i);
questions.explanation: The loop starts at 5 and decreases i by 1 until it reaches 1.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int sum = 0; for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) sum += i; printf("%d", sum);
What will be the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i += 2) printf("%d ", i);
questions.explanation: The loop starts at 1 and increases by 2, producing 1, 3 and 5.

questions.questionText: Which of the following creates an infinite for loop in C?
questions.explanation: A for loop with all three expressions omitted, written as for (;;), has no termination condition and is an infinite loop unless terminated internally.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int i = 1; while (i <= 5) { if (i == 4) break; printf("%d ", i); i++; }
questions.explanation: When i becomes 4, break executes before printf, so only 1, 2 and 3 are printed.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { if (i % 2 == 0) continue; printf("%d ", i); }
questions.explanation: The continue statement skips even values of i, so only the odd values 1, 3 and 5 are printed.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? for (int i = 1; i <= 2; i++) { for (int j = 1; j <= 2; j++) printf("%d%d ", i, j); }
questions.explanation: For i = 1, j produces 11 and 12. For i = 2, j produces 21 and 22.

questions.questionText: What will be the output? int i = 1; do { printf("%d ", i); i++; } while (i <= 3);
questions.explanation: The do-while loop prints 1, 2 and 3 before the condition becomes false.

questions.questionText: Which statement is true about the three basic loops in C?
questions.optionA: Only for loop can be used for repetition
questions.optionB: while loop always executes at least once
questions.optionC: do-while loop executes its body before checking the condition
questions.optionD: for loop cannot have a condition
questions.explanation: In a do-while loop, the loop body is executed first and the condition is checked afterward.
